pages.title: File:Antakya Church of St. Peter exterior ın 2025 05.jpg

ObjectName.value: Antakya Church of St. Peter exterior ın 2025 05

Categories.value: Church of Saint Peter|Self-published work|2019 in Antakya

ImageDescription.value: The early Gothic facade was erected by the Crusaders (restored in 1863). The interior was transformed into a three aisle church. Some remains of a mosaic floor are fifth century. To the left of the altar is a - now caved-in, tunnel early Christians would use to flee in case the authorities were after them. To the right of the altar is a font with water dripping down the rocks that is supposedly medicinal. It sued to be called for paptisms. A notice inside indicates that Pope Paul VI paid the place a visit and promised a plenary indulgence to whoever came here.
